summary: A toggle for an on/off setting with its label, description and error laid out beside it, taking part in forms.

label.note: Visible label next to the track and accessible name. Required: shadow DOM keeps an external <label for> from reaching the inner input.

hideLabel.note: Visually hides the label; it stays the accessible name. Use only when the row has other visible text naming the switch.

error.note: Error message. Setting it marks the field invalid and sets a customError validity.

value.note: Submitted with the form while on.

checked.note: Current on/off state. Not reflected: the attribute is the default restored by form reset.

required.note: Native required: the switch must be on. Adds an aria-hidden asterisk after the label.

disabled.note: Native disabled; dimmed; not submitted. A disabled ancestor fieldset also disables it without changing this attribute.

anatomy.name: field
anatomy.notes: Grid: track in the first column, label, description and error in the second.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: Track wrapper; the thumb moves inside it.

anatomy.name: input
anatomy.notes: Native <input type="checkbox" role="switch">; receives focus, Space and validation.

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.notes: Native <label for> in the same shadow root.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: Persistent polite live region; text appears when invalid.

input.note: Each toggle. Native and composed, so it crosses the shadow boundary.

change.note: Toggle committed. Re-dispatched from the host because native change is not composed (NativeControl).

focus-visible.note: 3px solid ring around the track (a translucent ring would fall under 3:1).

checked.note: Track in primary, thumb moved to the logical end (the left in RTL).

invalid.trigger: error set, or required and off after blur or a submit attempt

disabled.trigger: disabled attribute or disabled ancestor fieldset

accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop, through a native <label for> in the same shadow root.

formAssociation.note: ElementInternals via FormAssociated + NativeControl: setFormValue(value) only while on (null when off), validity mirrored from the inner input (required -> valueMissing, error -> customError), formResetCallback restores the checked attribute default, formStateRestore restores the saved state; a disabled control or disabled fieldset is not submitted and re-enabling restores operation.

accessibility.targetSize: The track is 32x20px (24x16px at sm); the label is part of the clickable row, and the 12px gap satisfies the WCAG 2.5.8 spacing exception.
accessibility.focusRingVisible: On keyboard focus of the input; 3px ring in switch.focus-ring.color.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: Dev-only console warning, once, when label is empty.

keyboard.Tab: move focus to and from the switch
keyboard.Enter: submits the form (implicit submission; the control has no form owner in its shadow root, SB-0009); it does not toggle

aria: role="switch" on the native checkbox; its checked state is the on/off state, no aria-checked set by hand
aria-describedby -> description and error ids (same root)
required: native required; the asterisk is aria-hidden
error: sets a customError validity, so the form blocks submission
announcements: error text is announced once when it appears (persistent aria-live=polite region)
the state change is announced by the switch role itself; no extra live text

useCases.when: A setting that is on or off, such as notifications
useCases.use: sb-switch with a label that names the setting

useCases.when: The consequence of the setting needs explaining
The setting must be on before the form can be sent
useCases.use: required with a label that states the condition

useCases.when: A dense row or list of settings

antiPatterns.pattern: A choice that is only recorded when the form is submitted, such as consent
antiPatterns.why: A switch reads as an on/off setting; a recorded choice reads as a checkbox

antiPatterns.pattern: Choosing exactly one option from several
antiPatterns.why: A switch is one independent on/off value
The label is the only name for the control
antiPatterns.alternative: A label that names the setting

coverage: label is the name; role switch; label click toggles
Space toggles; Enter submits and does not toggle; keyboard focus ring
checked paints differently; thumb moves, mirrored in RTL
description and error in the accessible description; aria-invalid
required: native required, aria-hidden asterisk, invalid after blur
input and change composed, once per toggle
form value only while on, custom value, reset to attribute default, state restore, validity, disabled fieldset and re-enable, error customError, label for

drift.contract: label, description and error are props of Switch
drift.realization: shadcn composes Field parts around Switch; shadow DOM requires them inside

drift.contract: color.input for the off track (3:1 against the background)
drift.realization: shadcn uses a lighter input color; changed for WCAG 1.4.11
not reflected: the attribute is the default restored by form reset

openQuestions.question: Where do label, description and error live?
openQuestions.answer: Inside Switch (recommended, as Checkbox and Input): native <label for>, description and error in one shadow root.

openQuestions.question: Is label required?
openQuestions.answer: Yes (recommended, as Checkbox). hide-label keeps it as the accessible name.

openQuestions.question: Is checked reflected to an attribute?
openQuestions.answer: No (recommended, as Checkbox). The attribute is the default that form reset restores.

openQuestions.question: Which sizes, and under which names?
openQuestions.answer: Two: default (32x20) and sm (24x16), through the registered size alias (default=medium, sm=small).

openQuestions.question: Does Enter toggle or submit?
openQuestions.answer: Submit. APG makes Enter optional for a switch; the form-control standard (SB-0009) has Enter request form submission. Only Space toggles.

openQuestions.question: Is the role native or ARIA?
openQuestions.answer: A native checkbox input with role=switch (recommended): keeps native checked, validity and Space behavior.

openQuestions.question: Does the thumb mirror in RTL?
openQuestions.answer: Yes: the thumb moves to the logical end, read through :dir(rtl) (SB-0007).
